name: Sivan
role_or_note: Hassan's tribe; the interview says it had thirty-four villages.

name: Ahmed Beg
role_or_note: Mentioned in Hassan's list of feuds: the feud between Ahmed Beg and Sivan.

name: Ali Beg of Aldun
role_or_note: Named as the elder of Aldun.
follow_up: Check against Ottoman/local records for Aldun and surrounding Palu/Genç material.

name: Avdula Beg
role_or_note: Mentioned in Hassan's list of feuds he saw: the feud between Sivan and Avdula Beg.
follow_up: Compare with the Avdulah Agha of Kelan in the Sivan-Nyêrib story.

name: Hassan
role_or_note: Primary Zaza-speaking consultant for the processed Lerch Zazaki texts; says his tribe is Sivan and his village is Kasan/Kassau/Kaschan.
source_basis: Hassan interview text; Lerch collection intro notes
follow_up: Confirm the modern location of Kasan/Kassau/Kaschan and whether living descendants connect to this village name.

name: Mistefa Ali
role_or_note: Named as the elder of Gewel.

name: Kasan / Kassau / Kaschan
role_or_note: Hassan's village; described as having sixty houses in the interview.
source_basis: Hassan interview text; Lerch collection intro notes
follow_up: High-priority place identification; keep all spellings together until externally resolved.

name: Sivan village list
role_or_note: The interview gives a list of Sivan villages: Fatrakom, Hopsor, Tenik, Rezuan, Zimag, Horsig, Hemek, Bilike, Melekan, Mark, Aldun, Gewel, Kasan, Hoena, Sama, Emera, Shekera, Heylan, Mala-Ibrahiman, Avdelan, Mistan, Sayere, Abasa, Wisheyn, Haspeg, Seratyori, Akeragi, Letan, Gahar, Gowman, Kavare, Talek.
follow_up: Split into individually researched modern place rows after external checking.

name: Ziriki aghas
role_or_note: Asked by Daqma Beg to mediate; they bring Daqma Beg to Xalef Ağa's house and the feud ends with compensation/exchange.
follow_up: Potentially useful for researching regional beylik networks.

name: Daqma Beg
role_or_note: Hyêni leader opposing Xalef Ağa; gathers his army near Temir Beg's house and later makes peace through the Ziriki aghas.
follow_up: Check whether Daqma Beg can be identified in external Hani/Hyêni records.

name: Mela Haseynê Mûğara
role_or_note: The first Hyêni man killed is described as his servant; the killer says Mela Haseynê Mûğara had killed one of his grandfather's servants earlier.

name: Mêhmêt Ağa of Deştê Henzi
role_or_note: Receives warning through Wesman Ağa and reports readiness for the expected Hyêni attack.

name: Temir Beg / Timur Bey of Hani
role_or_note: The story mentions Temir Beg's house as a gathering point. Local research notes identify a likely match with Timur/Temir Bey of Hani, active by 1819 and defeated/exiled in 1835.
source_basis: Nerib-Hyêni text; local external-source research note
follow_up: Verify the identification in the cited Ottoman/dissertation/Brant sources before making a firm historical claim.

name: Wesman Ağa
role_or_note: Agha of Little Nerib; Xalef sends him word to warn Mehmet Agha.

name: Xalef Ağa
role_or_note: Nerib leader in the Nerib-Hyêni feud; receives the report of the first killing, organizes the Nerib side, fights Daqma Beg, and later makes peace.
follow_up: Also appears in the Sivan-Nyêrib story; compare chronology across the two narratives.

name: Xalil Efendi
role_or_note: Killed during the attack on Hyêni; his head is taken to Xalef Ağa.

name: Deştê Henzi
role_or_note: Place tied to Mehmet Ağa and also appears in the Sivan-Nyêrib story.

name: Hyêni / Hêni / Hani / Khini
role_or_note: Main opposing territory/town in the Nerib-Hyêni feud; connected in working notes with Hani and Temir/Timur Bey.
follow_up: Use Hani as a working modern Turkish identification only with caveat.

name: Nyêrib
role_or_note: Nerib-side home territory and Xalef Ağa's base.

name: Working chronology: after Nerib-Hyêni, before/during 1853 collection horizon
role_or_note: The message to Xalef warns him not to come to Hyêni because he fought there, so this story seems later than the Nerib-Hyêni story. Since Lerch recorded the texts during the Crimean War period, the broad working range is roughly 1820-1853.
follow_up: Do not publish as a fixed date without external confirmation.

name: Avdulah Ağa of Kelan
role_or_note: Sivan-side leader; confronts Xalef Ağa, burns and plunders Nerib villages, and later grants reconciliation after Hayder Ağa intercedes.
follow_up: Compare with Hassan's mention of a feud between Sivan and Avdula Beg.

name: Hayder Ağa of Qotwesan
role_or_note: Mediates after Xalef Ağa's defeat; takes Xalef Ağa to Avdulah Ağa's house and secures reconciliation.
follow_up: Potentially important external research target because he acts as protector/mediator.

name: Huseyin, son of Mela Ahmed
role_or_note: Catches and kills the Nerib thief and sends word to Xalef Ağa.

name: Mela Ahmed Qafon
role_or_note: His house is robbed at the beginning of the story.

name: Xalef Ağa
role_or_note: Nerib leader in the Sivan-Nyêrib feud; threatens Avdulah Ağa after one of his men is killed, is later badly defeated, and seeks mediation through Hayder Ağa.
follow_up: Because this story appears to allude to the earlier Hyêni conflict, compare with the Xalef Ağa of the Nerib-Hyêni story.

name: Dait
role_or_note: Direction/place named as Xalef Ağa's side of the planned battle route.
follow_up: Needs modern identification.

name: Horsig
role_or_note: Sivan-associated place where the opening theft takes place.
source_basis: Sivan-Nyêrib text and Hassan interview village list

name: Kelan
role_or_note: Avdulah Ağa's place.

name: Sele stream
role_or_note: Battle rendezvous point named by Avdulah Ağa.
follow_up: Needs modern identification.

name: Ahmed, son of Ali Ağa
role_or_note: Warns against handing over weapons; obtains a dagger, attacks Qasım Ağa, kills Eysan and Hasan Kalan, then is killed.

name: Ali Ağa, son of Kelhan
role_or_note: Mir/chief of the Karbegan district; his village is Narbêş. The story says he killed thirty-four people and was later killed with his four sons.
follow_up: Search external Karbegan/Sivan feud references and possible Ottoman records.

name: Eysan
role_or_note: Killed by Ahmed in the fighting. Metadata should not be read as 'Ahmed Êysan' without checking; the English translation treats Eysan as a separate person.
follow_up: Review the exact line in Lerch before final public person table.

name: Hasan Kalan
role_or_note: Killed by Ahmed in the fighting.

name: Kelhan
role_or_note: Named as Ali Ağa's father in the title/patronymic.
source_basis: Ali Ağa title and opening line

name: Mela Qasım of Desmun
role_or_note: Helps recover and bury Ali Ağa, his sons, and the foreign men.

name: Mela Resa
role_or_note: Calls Mela Qasım of Desmun in the morning to remove and bury the dead.

name: Memed Ağa of Ğêytê
role_or_note: Helps recover and bury the bodies after the attack.

name: Qasım Ağa
role_or_note: Karbegan-side figure who plans the attack, deceives Ali Ağa into giving up weapons, and is stabbed by Ahmed. Ahmed addresses him as uncle/nephew language, but the exact kinship should be checked.
follow_up: Clarify kinship terminology from the Zazaki line before publishing as a family relation.

name: Ramedan Ağa of Merzyelê
role_or_note: Helps recover and bury the bodies after the attack.

name: Weşinli Hasan Ağa
role_or_note: Co-conspirator with Qasım Ağa in the attack on Ali Ağa.

name: Karbegan
role_or_note: District over which Ali Ağa is said to be mir/chief; later thirty-four Karbegan villages are involved in counsel.

name: Narbêş
role_or_note: Ali Ağa's village according to the story.
follow_up: Needs modern identification.

name: Syeraçur
role_or_note: Place where Ali Ağa stays for thirty-six days after packing up his household.
follow_up: Needs modern identification.

name: Weşin
role_or_note: Place associated with Hasan Ağa; also appears in Hassan's Sivan village list as Wisheyn/Weşin.
